title: Koszul self Ext is the dual of the exterior conormal
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], V an open of Z and n a natural number. Suppose that every z∈V has an affine neighborhood U of i(z) for which the ideal i.ker.ideal U [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is the span of a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put C=i*ker(i) using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], B=i_*O_Z, and G=H^n(RHom_Y(B[0],B[0])) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then the restriction to V of Hom_Z(exteriorSheaf(C,n),O_Z) [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power, def-pur-sheaf-hom] is isomorphic as an O_V-module to (i*G)|V. The conclusion concerns the dual of the exterior conormal, not an exterior power of the dual, and asserts no compatibility with Yoneda products.

source.place: duality.tex, lemma-regular-ideal-ext: Hom of the Koszul resolution into the quotient, its zero differential, and changes of generators; Tag 062I for I/I²

proof.text: On a regular affine chart resolve A/I by the actual augmented Koszul projective resolution. Sheafify its augmentation and use open restriction of derived internal Hom and the bounded-above finite-free Hom model. The differential of Hom(K,A/I) is zero, since every generator lies in I. Thus degree-n cohomology is Hom_A(wedge^n A^m,A/I), which equals Hom_(A/I)(wedge^n((A/I)^m),A/I).

Identify (A/I)^m with I/I² by the regular conormal basis. This identifies the preceding module with the dual of wedge^n(I/I²). Sheafifying identifies it with dual(exteriorSheaf C n) on the inverse-image chart, where C=i*ker(i). The quotient scalar action is the usual A/I action, so the tensor pullback after cohomology gives that same module.

For a substitution f′=A f use exteriorPower.map of the corresponding degree-one linear map in every Koszul degree. The contraction-sum formula shows it commutes with the differential and it lifts the identity of A/I. On reduction modulo I its degree-one map is exactly the map on conormal classes, and its degree-n map is their nth exterior power. Hom into A/I transposes this map, exactly the transition on the dual exterior conormal. Comparison maps lifting the identity of A/I are homotopic because both are projective resolutions; hence choices give identical cohomology maps. These formulas commute with localization. Refine intersections by affine subopens and glue the local maps and inverses by the sheaf condition. A common K-injective Hom model compares the given derived universe. Degree zero, degrees above the chart length, and empty V satisfy the same formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_dual_exterior_conormal
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (hregular : ∀ z : Z, z ∈ V → ∃ U : Y.affineOpens, i z ∈ U.1 ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let T := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G)
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      (Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules) n))
    Nonempty (F ≅ T)
